mechanism_narrative: The steady rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the last four weeks signals more daily trip-making, which should spill into higher retail and recreation visits within four weeks as commuting resumes and discretionary stopovers increase.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean even as WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising for two additional weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL continues falling while RETAIL_REC is still deeply negative, households are spending slightly less time at home and reallocating short trips toward errands and shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the next 1 to 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 30 and continues declining week-on-week
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines further but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days relative to the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in PARKS and TRANSIT indicates broader out-of-home activity and urban circulation; when both move up together, retail and recreation mobility should improve over the next four weeks as outings combine leisure and shopping.
failure_condition: PARKS and TRANSIT rise together but RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stop improving after their current downward gaps, the city is likely in a renewed restriction or weak-demand regime that suppresses discretionary outings, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses and drops more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall further, but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average within 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent collapse in PARKS use can act as a proxy for very weak discretionary outdoor demand; if PARKS remains extremely depressed, retail and recreation mobility should stay depressed or fall further over the next two weeks because the same outing constraint limits shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -90 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -90 for two weeks yet RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A gradual lift in GROCERY_PHARM alongside a smaller rise in RETAIL_REC suggests routine errand consolidation rather than broad reopening; when this pattern persists, retail mobility should edge up over four weeks as households batch essential and non-essential trips.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising but RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed while RESIDENTIAL is still elevated, the city is operating under mobility restraint that keeps discretionary retail trips contained; the next 1-week to 2-week change in RETAIL_REC should remain negative unless transit recovers first.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -75 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 25
failure_condition: TRANSIT stays below -75 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 25, but RETAIL_REC rises for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained narrowing gap between WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL indicates people are leaving home more often for work-related reasons, which should eventually pull retail visits upward over the next four weeks as commuting-based errands normalize.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls, yet RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week average after 28 days.
